potentially_qualify.title: Your answers may be worth a lawyer's review.
potentially_qualify.body: Based on what you told us, you may potentially qualify for a lawyer to review the facts. That is not a decision about your case. The next page belongs to a firm network that reviews this kind of matter.
potentially_qualify.note: You will leave DoIHaveAClaim.ai and continue to {{destination_host}}. Nothing you answered here is sent with you except campaign tracking codes.

potentially_qualify_sofia.title: Your answers may be worth a lawyer's review.
potentially_qualify_sofia.body: Based on what you told us, you may potentially qualify for a lawyer to review the facts. That is not a decision about your case. A network firm does not have a dedicated page for this matter yet, so Sofia takes it from here: she can explain what kind of firm handles it and whether one is accepting it.
potentially_qualify_sofia.note: Sofia is an AI assistant on this site. She cannot decide whether you have a claim, and she does not see your answers here.

injury.title: This sounds like an injury matter.
injury.body: Injury cases are handled through Nearest Injury Lawyers. Their team can talk through what happened and whether a firm is accepting matters like yours.
injury.note: You will leave DoIHaveAClaim.ai and continue to {{destination_host}}. Nothing you answered here is sent with you except campaign tracking codes.

no_match.title: This screen stopped here.
no_match.body: One of your answers is a common reason a reviewer would not take this further right now. That is not a legal decision, and it does not mean you have no options. If you want a second look, talk it through with Sofia.
no_match.note: Sofia is an AI assistant on this site. She cannot decide whether you have a claim.

closed.title: A new claim is not open for this.
closed.body: The Navy's Camp Lejeune Justice Act deadline was August 10, 2024, and the Navy is not taking new claims. This screen cannot tell you a new claim is possible. If you believe a claim was filed for you or a family member before that date, Sofia can help you sort out where that file stands.
closed.note: The government never asks a claimant for money. A call or email that asks for payment is not part of any claim.

unsure.title: Let's talk it through instead.
unsure.body: This short screen is built for a few specific matters. Yours may need a conversation. Sofia can ask better follow-ups and explain what kind of firm usually handles situations like yours.
unsure.note: Sofia is an AI assistant on this site. She cannot decide whether you have a claim.

stop_reasons.no_occupational_exposure: The screen looks for work around a restricted farm herbicide: spraying, mixing, loading, or working beside people who did.
stop_reasons.no_parkinsons_diagnosis: The screen looks for a Parkinson's disease diagnosis made by a doctor. A tremor without a diagnosis, or a different movement disorder, is not the same answer.
stop_reasons.diagnosis_before_exposure: The screen looks for a diagnosis that came after the exposure or use.
stop_reasons.already_settled: A claim that was already settled or released is normally not reviewed again.
stop_reasons.afff_no_exposure: The screen looks for real contact with the foam or contaminated drinking water as part of daily life: firefighting, training drills, or living and working where the water was affected. A brief visit or living somewhere near a base is a weak screen.
stop_reasons.afff_no_listed_diagnosis: The conditions that most often move an AFFF screen forward are kidney cancer, testicular cancer, thyroid cancer, thyroid disease, ulcerative colitis, and liver cancer, diagnosed by a doctor.
stop_reasons.afff_property_only: A water bill, a property, or a utility question is a different kind of case from a personal illness.
stop_reasons.clja_not_filed: The Navy's Camp Lejeune Justice Act deadline was August 10, 2024. A claim that was not filed by then cannot be started now.
stop_reasons.clja_under_30_days: The statute requires at least 30 days at Camp Lejeune or Marine Corps Air Station New River between August 1, 1953 and December 31, 1987.
stop_reasons.clja_outside_window: Time on base only outside August 1, 1953 through December 31, 1987 does not meet the screen.
stop_reasons.clja_no_listed_diagnosis: The government's Elective Option uses nine conditions: kidney cancer, liver cancer, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, leukemias, bladder cancer, multiple myeloma, Parkinson's disease, kidney disease (stage 4, stage 5, or end-stage), and systemic sclerosis.
stop_reasons.clja_released: A Camp Lejeune claim that was already settled and released is closed.
stop_reasons.rd_single_use: The screen looks for the person's own repeated use, or a job that put them in the spray again and again. A one-time spray, or a park where someone else once sprayed, is a weak screen.
stop_reasons.rd_no_nhl: The screen looks for a doctor's diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma or one of its subtypes. Hodgkin lymphoma and solid tumors are different diagnoses.
stop_reasons.rd_prior_settlement: Someone who already joined an earlier Roundup settlement and released this cancer is normally not reviewed again.
stop_reasons.hm_no_mesh: These cases are about a mesh patch. A hernia repaired with stitches only is not the same fact pattern.
stop_reasons.hm_no_complication: Firms usually want a complication tied to the mesh, most often another surgery, infection, obstruction, adhesions, a fistula, or erosion. Ordinary soreness or a hernia coming back, on its own, is a common weak screen.
stop_reasons.hm_released: A claim about this implant that was already settled or released is normally not reviewed again.
stop_reasons.talc_brief_use: The screen looks for regular talc use over a real stretch of years. Brief or occasional use is a weak screen.
stop_reasons.talc_cornstarch_only: Cornstarch powder is not the exposure this screen is about. Talc baby powder was no longer sold in the U.S. after 2020.
stop_reasons.talc_no_diagnosis: The screen looks for a doctor's diagnosis of ovarian cancer (including fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer) or mesothelioma. A family history, a BRCA result, or a worry is not a diagnosis.
stop_reasons.talc_asbestos_job: When the main exposure was an asbestos job such as shipyards, insulation, or brake work, that may be an asbestos case, which is a different matter from talc.
stop_reasons.talc_released: A talc claim that was already settled, released, or filed by another firm is normally not reviewed again here.

steps.prompt: What happened?
steps.help: Pick the closest fit. You can change your answer.

choices.label: I used or worked around a chemical, product, or powder, or had an implant, and was later diagnosed with an illness
I was hurt in an accident — car, fall, work, or something similar
Something else, or I'm not sure

steps.prompt: Which product or exposure was it?
steps.help: Pick the one that fits best. Each has its own short set of questions.

choices.label: Paraquat or Gramoxone — a licensed farm herbicide
Roundup or another glyphosate weed killer
AFFF firefighting foam, or drinking water contaminated by it
Talc baby powder (Johnson's, Shower to Shower, or similar)
A different product, or I don't know the name

steps.prompt: Did your work include spraying, mixing, or loading a restricted farm herbicide, or working beside people who did?
steps.help: Farmers, farmworkers, licensed applicators, commercial landscapers, and some grounds crews are the usual fits.

choices.label: Yes — I sprayed, mixed, or loaded it
Yes — I worked in fields, orchards, groves, or grounds while others sprayed it
It was actually Roundup or a store-bought yard spray

steps.prompt: About what years were you around it?
steps.help: A rough answer is fine. A reviewer decides how much exposure is enough; this screen does not.

steps.prompt: About how often were you around it?
steps.help: Think about a typical season of that work.

choices.label: Seasonally — a few weeks a year

steps.prompt: Has a doctor diagnosed you with Parkinson's disease?
steps.help: This is not a medical exam. We only need to know whether a doctor made the diagnosis.

choices.label: I have a tremor or symptoms, but no diagnosis

steps.prompt: Was that diagnosis made after the work around the herbicide?
Have you already settled or released a paraquat claim?
Did you personally spray or mix Roundup, or another glyphosate weed killer, more than once?

choices.label: Yes — it was part of my job
Once, or I was only near someone else's spraying

steps.prompt: Where was that?

choices.label: At home, in the yard or garden
At a job such as landscaping, grounds, golf, or parks

steps.prompt: About what years did you use it?
steps.help: Use can run from the 1970s through recent years. A reviewer decides how much is enough.

steps.prompt: About how often?

choices.label: A few times a month in season

steps.prompt: Has a doctor diagnosed non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or a subtype of it?
steps.help: Subtypes include diffuse large B-cell, follicular, CLL/SLL, mantle cell, and marginal zone lymphoma.

choices.label: Yes — non-Hodgkin lymphoma or a subtype
Hodgkin lymphoma, or a different cancer

steps.prompt: Was that diagnosis made after you had been using the product?
Were you already part of an earlier Roundup settlement?
How were you around AFFF foam?
steps.help: Firefighter cases and drinking-water cases are different fact patterns.

choices.label: I was a firefighter (career, volunteer, airport, industrial, or military) who trained with or sprayed it
I served in the military and took part in drills where it was used
I lived or worked where drinking water was contaminated by the foam
A brief visit, or I lived somewhere near a base
My question is about a water bill, a property, or a utility

steps.prompt: About what years?
steps.help: AFFF with PFAS was used from about the 1960s into the 2000s, and in some places later.

steps.prompt: Has a doctor diagnosed one of these conditions?
steps.help: Kidney cancer, testicular cancer, thyroid cancer, thyroid disease, ulcerative colitis, or liver cancer.

steps.prompt: Was that diagnosis made after the exposure?
Have you already settled a claim for this same illness?
Were you at Camp Lejeune or Marine Corps Air Station New River for at least 30 days between August 1, 1953 and December 31, 1987?
steps.help: Living there, working there, or in the womb while your mother did all count.

choices.label: Yes — at least 30 days in that window
A different base, or I'm not sure

steps.prompt: Did you, or the person who died, receive a doctor's diagnosis of one of the nine listed conditions?
steps.help: Kidney cancer, liver cancer, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, leukemias, bladder cancer, multiple myeloma, Parkinson's disease, kidney disease (stage 4, 5, or end-stage), or systemic sclerosis.

steps.prompt: Was a Camp Lejeune Justice Act claim actually filed with the Navy by August 10, 2024?

choices.label: Not sure — a lawyer or family member may have

steps.prompt: Where does that claim stand?
Did a surgeon repair your hernia with a mesh patch?
Do you know the brand, or have an implant card or operative report?
steps.help: A reviewer needs the records. The brand cannot be guessed.

choices.label: I have the implant card or operative report

steps.prompt: After that surgery, what happened?

choices.label: I had another operation to remove, replace, or revise the mesh
A doctor found infection, bowel obstruction, adhesions, a fistula, or erosion tied to the mesh
Pain or the hernia came back, but no revision and no doctor tying it to the mesh

steps.prompt: About what year was the mesh put in?
Have you already settled a claim about this implant?
Did you use Johnson's baby powder, Shower to Shower, or another talc body powder on a regular basis for years?
How did you use it?
Was the powder a talc formula?
steps.help: Johnson & Johnson switched U.S. baby powder to cornstarch in 2020.

choices.label: Yes, talc — or my use was mostly before 2020
Cornstarch only, or use started after 2020

steps.prompt: About how many years?
Has a doctor diagnosed one of these?

choices.label: Ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary peritoneal cancer
No diagnosis — a worry, a family history, or a BRCA result only

steps.prompt: Was your main exposure an asbestos job, such as shipyards, insulation, or brake work?
Was that diagnosis made after the years of use?
Have you already settled a talc claim, or did a law firm already file one for you?
When did the accident happen?
